de-0QTU.title: Postal codes: counter-clockwise from 0 to 9
de-0QTU.summary: Postal codes run counter-clockwise, from 0 around Saxony to 9 in northern Bavaria and parts of Thuringia.

de-0fgb.title: Flags: each state has its own
de-0fgb.summary: Each state has its own flag, but many are rare to find.

de-1NkZ.title: Language: Ä Ö Ü and ß
de-1NkZ.summary: German uses the letters Ä, Ö, Ü and ß. Switzerland, Austria and Liechtenstein also speak it, as do East Belgium and South Tyrol.

de-1pPN.title: Google car: Gen 3 with antenna in the city
de-1pPN.summary: Rare Gen 3 car coverage with an antenna in central Hamburg.

de-2QHh.title: Sign: black or dark grey sign backs
de-2QHh.summary: A wide variety of sign backs, notably black or dark grey ones, which are rare in Europe. Most carry a sticker with an upside-down red triangle on a black rectangle. Italy, Romania and Albania have black backs too.

de-2hc8.title: Pole: round concrete
de-2hc8.summary: Round concrete poles are almost unique to the former East.

de-443T.title: Bollard: round wooden with painted top
de-443T.summary: Round wooden bollards with a painted top are found in Bavaria.

de-4rEl.title: Bus stop: big yellow and green H
de-4rEl.summary: Many regional bus stop designs, all with a big yellow and green H. Austria does the same.

de-6qzp.title: Sign: pedestrian sign with 5 stripes and a belt
de-6qzp.summary: Pedestrian signs have five stripes and the person wears a belt. Luxembourg uses the same design.

de-6w4I.title: Landscape: the only high mountains, Austrian border
de-6w4I.summary: The Alps are the most mountainous region, mostly along the Austrian border.

de-7lT0.title: Google car: Gen 4 for all car coverage
de-7lT0.summary: All car coverage is the Gen 4 camera. There are some older Gen 2 and 3 trekkers and older spill coverage.

de-8CJo.title: Town names: -ow and -itz east, -weiler and -ach south
de-8CJo.summary: Useful place name endings. Slavic-origin -ow and -itz are mainly in the east, while -weiler and -ach are mainly in the southern half.

de-8sZa.title: Route marker: simple rectangle with rounded corners
de-8sZa.summary: Simple rectangular markers with rounded edges are in Lower Saxony.

de-8xMd.title: Bollard: triangular posts by region
de-8xMd.summary: Triangular posts vary by state. Rhineland-Palatinate and Saxony have unpainted rocky-looking posts with white plates. Saarland, Thuringia and Baden-Württemberg have white posts with white plates (shorter in BW), and BW also has grey ones. North Rhine-Westphalia has white posts without plates.

de-9QQL.title: Trees: tiny green tags
de-9QQL.summary: Many trees in the northeast (Brandenburg and Mecklenburg-Vorpommern) have tiny green markers. Very rarely in Lower Saxony.

de-B2L8.title: Shops: Aldi Süd in the south, Aldi Nord in the north
de-B2L8.summary: Two regional Aldi chains split the country: Aldi Süd in the south and Aldi Nord in the north.

de-EHw4.title: Bollard: green cap with 'LVR' and coat of arms
de-EHw4.summary: Some green caps carry the text LVR and a small coat of arms, unique to the southern part of North Rhine-Westphalia.

de-Eveq.title: Google car: Gen 3 black car in a safari park
de-Eveq.summary: A Gen 3 black car in a safari park southeast of Bielefeld, with 4x4s painted with zebra stripes. This car is unique to the park in all of Europe.

de-FDU2.title: Sign: street sign backs, folded or flat
de-FDU2.summary: Backs of street signs help to guess the region. Examples show a folded and a flat back.

de-FIDL.title: Pole: bar with a thicker middle
de-FIDL.summary: Pole tops where the middle of the horizontal bar is thicker are across the former East. Similar poles exist elsewhere, so be careful.

de-FfPz.title: Landscape: shrubby sandy hills on an island
de-FfPz.summary: Shrub and sand covered hills are unique to the island of Sylt. Like other North Frisian Islands it has stone walls, brick houses and thatched roofs. Parts look more generic but still very flat.

de-H6Lb.title: Coverage: lowcam near Switzerland
de-H6Lb.summary: Low-mounted camera coverage is found around Singen and near Switzerland.

de-KfVL.title: Landscape: flat north, hilly middle, Alps south
de-KfVL.summary: The north, especially the northwest, is very flat. The centre is hilly, and the far south has big mountains, though many southern parts are flat despite being high.

de-KxEL.title: Bollard: yellow post with a white plate
de-KxEL.summary: Yellow posts with a white plate are in Saxony-Anhalt. With only one plate they are hard to tell from Brandenburg's.

de-LIr8.title: Bollard: black and white, white-grey reflector
de-LIr8.summary: Black and white bollards with white and light-grey reflectors, orange next to intersections. They may have road number plates and blue side attachments. Luxembourg's are almost identical but have 3 bolts on the reflector instead of 2.

de-LVZN.title: Mailbox: bright yellow with black logo
de-LVZN.summary: Bright yellow mailboxes with a black logo.

de-Lhfc.title: Route marker: white, split by black lines in three
de-Lhfc.summary: Bavaria's white rectangular markers are divided by black lines into three sections. The left section shows the road you're on.

de-Lxxs.title: Pole: curved horizontal bar
de-Lxxs.summary: Pole tops with a curved horizontal bar exist in Bavaria, but are rare.

de-MPmF.title: Houses: half-timbered with ground-floor arches
de-MPmF.summary: Half-timbered houses with arches on the ground floor are very common in one part of Saxony.

de-O4bv.title: Guardrail: B-type mostly, A-type in the west
de-O4bv.summary: Most of the country uses B-type guardrails, but A-type is common in the northwest, in Rhineland-Palatinate and parts of Bavaria. Exceptions always exist.

de-ONji.title: Bollard: fully yellow posts
de-ONji.summary: Fully yellow posts are found in Brandenburg.

de-OO0W.title: Sign: one-way sign saying Einbahnstraße
de-OO0W.summary: One-way signs with the full word 'Einbahnstraße' are unique. Austria's say just 'EINBAHN'.

de-SDqs.title: Street sign: city-by-city designs
de-SDqs.summary: Big cities have their own street signs: Berlin white with a grey border and a number box, Munich blue with a decorative white border, Stuttgart black without border, Düsseldorf black with white border and metal frame, Dortmund, Essen, Dresden, Nuremberg and Frankfurt blue variants, Hanover and Wu…

de-T3Bx.title: Car: round sticker on windscreen, usually green
de-T3Bx.summary: Almost every car has a round, usually green sticker at the bottom right of the windscreen with a 4 on it. Rarely yellow (3) or red (2).

de-VVId.title: Houses: black slate walls like fish scales
de-VVId.summary: Houses with black slate walls that look like fish scales are common over a large area of central Germany.

de-Yoh4.title: Sign: street sign back connectors
de-Yoh4.summary: The connectors on street sign backs also help with the region. Double connectors on triangular signs are usually wider, and T-shaped connectors exist.

de-ZowM.title: Language: Slavic Sorbian near Poland and Czech border
de-ZowM.summary: Sorbian, a Slavic language, appears on various signs near the Polish and Czech borders.

de-aFr3.title: Plate: state coat of arms on unblurred plates
de-aFr3.summary: Each state has its own coat of arms, seen on unblurred plates and some official buildings.

de-agJb.title: Bollard: simple orange posts
de-agJb.summary: Simple orange posts are most common in Bavaria and a few other highlighted states.

de-dJN6.title: Bollard: one every 50 metres
de-dJN6.summary: An excessive number of bollards on most roads, about every 50 metres.

de-dPiq.title: Landscape: flat farmland with a ridge to the NE
de-dPiq.summary: The flat plains southeast of Regensburg are very agricultural, often with a slight ridge to the northeast.

de-e2UJ.title: Bollard: white post with red cap
de-e2UJ.summary: White posts with a red cap are across the former East, most often in Saxony-Anhalt.

de-evf5.title: Bollard: green cap on top in the west
de-evf5.summary: Some bollards in North Rhine-Westphalia have a green top, sometimes another colour.

de-fnjg.title: Plants: hop fields
de-fnjg.summary: Hop fields are common just north of Munich, mainly between Ingolstadt and Landshut, with minor areas in the east.

de-fv7n.title: Google car: rare white and black Gen 4 car
de-fv7n.summary: A rare white and black Gen 4 car in Hamburg and around Frankfurt. The same car is around London and in Ireland.

de-fv9L.title: Lamp post: yellow numbers on black plastic
de-fv9L.summary: Lamp posts in Cologne often have bright yellow numbers on a black plastic piece. Similar ones exist elsewhere.

de-gUz2.title: Plants: vineyards, mostly southwest
de-gUz2.summary: Vineyards are mostly in the southwest, with a few more regions further east (Thuringia and Saxony-Anhalt border, Elbe in Saxony). There are 13 wine regions.

de-gWFG.title: Sign: no stopping signs with white arrows
de-gWFG.summary: 'No Stopping' and 'No Waiting' signs often have white arrows drawn on them.

de-iPnK.title: Landmark: wind turbines everywhere
de-iPnK.summary: Wind turbines are much more common than in any other European country.

de-iiZK.title: Sign: yellow town entry with metal frame
de-iiZK.summary: Yellow town entry signs with black text and a metal frame. They show the town on top, the municipality in the middle and the county at the bottom.

de-jGsh.title: Plants: Scots pine with orange trunks, northeast
de-jGsh.summary: Scots pines, with orange-tinged trunks, are mostly in the northeast. The map is approximate.

de-jrD6.title: Pole: many pole tops, bar or triangle or T
de-jrD6.summary: A wide variety of poles. Common tops are a horizontal bar with uneven hanging insulators, a triangle, and many T-shaped tops.

de-lm-295800.title: Town names: Weiler on yellow or black signs
de-lm-295800.summary: In the southwest many villages have 'Weiler' in the name. Small villages' signs are sometimes yellow on green, bigger ones black on yellow.

de-lm-295804.title: Town names: -by ending
de-lm-295804.summary: In the north-east of Schleswig-Holstein, 49 places end in -by.

de-lm-295808.title: Town names: -hoven ending
de-lm-295808.summary: Southwest of Düsseldorf and around Bonn, 36 places end in -hoven.

de-lm-295809.title: Town names: -rath ending
de-lm-295809.summary: In western North Rhine-Westphalia, parts of Rhineland-Palatinate and Saarland, 144 places end in -rath.

de-lm-295811.title: Houses: wooden shingle walls (Schindeln)
de-lm-295811.summary: Wooden shingles called Schindeln are common on older farmhouses and traditional buildings in the south.

de-lm-295814.title: Traffic light: yellow bands
de-lm-295814.summary: Traffic lights in Bielefeld have yellow bands around them all over the city.

de-lm-295819.title: Houses: big with wooden details and flower balconies
de-lm-295819.summary: In the south: big houses with traditional wooden details, often with flower-covered balconies.

de-lm-295829.title: Town names: -itz ending
de-lm-295829.summary: In the east many towns end in -itz.

de-lm-295830.title: Streets: tram rails in the middle
de-lm-295830.summary: Many roads in Stuttgart have tram rails in the middle.

de-lm-295841.title: Sign: special signposts for crossings
de-lm-295841.summary: North Rhine-Westphalia sometimes uses unique signposts for pedestrian crossings. Rare but unique.

de-lm-295843.title: Houses: orange-brown brick near the French border
de-lm-295843.summary: Orange-brownish brick houses are west of Mannheim, to the French border.

de-lm-295846.title: Bus stop: blue, rounded top, name boards
de-lm-295846.summary: The big southern city uses blue bus stops with a rounded top and side boards showing the stop names, useful for regionguessing.

de-lm-295847.title: Town names: -ried ending
de-lm-295847.summary: Names ending in -ried are in parts of the southern half.

de-lm-295848.title: Bus: blue with MVG and the city coat of arms
de-lm-295848.summary: Trams and buses in Munich are mostly blue with MVG printed on them, often with the city coat of arms at the front. Trams can have large ads.

de-lm-295849.title: Church: rounded tower top
de-lm-295849.summary: Bavarian churches often have a rounded top on the tower. Rarely also in Baden-Württemberg.

de-lm-295853.title: Bollard: red, rare
de-lm-295853.summary: A red bollard is rarely found in Saxony-Anhalt.

de-lm-295856.title: Pole: round concrete with metal straps
de-lm-295856.summary: A round concrete pole with metal straps is most common in Saxony and generally in the east.

de-lm-295860.title: Town names: -ach ending
de-lm-295860.summary: In the southern half many towns end in -ach.

de-lm-295862.title: Town names: -ow ending
de-lm-295862.summary: In the north-east many towns end in -ow.

de-lm-295867.title: Bus: green, orange and white with MVB
de-lm-295867.summary: Magdeburg uses green (orange) and white trams and buses with MVB in a special font. They can be red but always show MVB. Trams can have large ads.

de-lm-295871.title: Houses: low roofs, long balconies in the forest
de-lm-295871.summary: In rural central-south parts of the Black Forest, a unique style with often low roofs and long balconies.

de-lm-295873.title: Shops: Fristo drink market
de-lm-295873.summary: Fristo is a drink market chain, common in the south and east, recognised by its unique sign visible from roads.

de-lm-295874.title: Town names: -stetten ending
de-lm-295874.summary: Names ending in -stetten are in the southern half.

de-lm-295875.title: Town names: -beck ending
de-lm-295875.summary: Names ending in -beck are in the northern half.

de-lm-295877.title: Town names: -hofen ending
de-lm-295877.summary: Names ending in -hofen are in the southern half.

de-lm-295878.title: Guardrail: looped end
de-lm-295878.summary: A loop at the end of the guardrail is common in Brandenburg, Berlin and Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, especially Brandenburg.

de-lm-295880.title: Town names: -scheid ending
de-lm-295880.summary: In western North Rhine-Westphalia, parts of Rhineland-Palatinate and Saarland, 195 places end in -scheid, and only 3 elsewhere.

de-lm-295891.title: Town names: -büll ending
de-lm-295891.summary: In the north-west of Schleswig-Holstein next to the Danish border, 30 places end in -büll.

de-lm-295893.title: Bus stop: blue with green frame, MVV
de-lm-295893.summary: Around Munich (13 districts) a unique blue bus stop with a green frame and MVV at the bottom. Not common in the city itself.

de-lm-2992.title: Sign: pedestrian figure with belt above hip
de-lm-2992.summary: Germany: belt above the hip, flat side of the arm on the left, pointed shoes. Hungary: belt at the bottom of the hip and flat side on the right. White belt also in Croatia and Portugal.

differs.how: belt lower on hip, flat side of arm on the right

de-lm-334178.title: Town names: -schütz ending
de-lm-334178.summary: Names ending in -schütz are in the east.

de-lm-334179.title: Town names: -itzsch ending
de-lm-334179.summary: Names ending in -itzsch are in the east.

de-lm-334181.title: Town names: -a ending
de-lm-334181.summary: Names ending in -a are in the southern half.

de-lm-334182.title: Town names: -weiler ending
de-lm-334182.summary: Names ending in -weiler are mainly in Rhineland-Palatinate, Saarland and Baden-Württemberg.

de-lm-334184.title: Guardrail: where A-type does not occur
de-lm-334184.summary: A-type guardrail is not found in the east, Hesse, Baden-Württemberg and Saarland.

de-lm-334185.title: Guardrail: where B-type does not occur
de-lm-334185.summary: B-type guardrail is not found in Schleswig-Holstein, Rhineland-Palatinate, Bremen and Hamburg.

de-lm-334188.title: Sign: bike signs with different arrow shapes
de-lm-334188.summary: The northern state sometimes uses different cycling sign designs: on the one with town names the arrow differs, on the one without the shape differs.

de-lm-334189.title: Sign back: folded
de-lm-334189.summary: Folded sign backs are most common in Bremen, then Saxony-Anhalt and Saarland.

de-lm-334190.title: Sign back: not folded
de-lm-334190.summary: Flat sign backs are most common in Schleswig-Holstein, Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, Hesse, Hamburg and Bremen, then Brandenburg, Saxony and Baden-Württemberg.

de-lm-334191.title: Sign back: T-shaped connector
de-lm-334191.summary: The T-shaped sign back connector is only in Hamburg.

de-lm-334192.title: Sign back: double connector
de-lm-334192.summary: The double connector is very common in Schleswig-Holstein and Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, also Brandenburg, and rarely Saxony, Rhineland-Palatinate or Hamburg.

de-lm-438610.title: Phone numbers: area code by region
de-lm-438610.summary: Area codes: 02 in the west, 03 in the east, 04 to 07 from northwest to southwest and 08 and 09 in the southeast. Numbers starting 01 are mobiles.

de-lm-440416.title: Bollard: darker reflectors
de-lm-440416.summary: Bollards with darker reflectors than usual are common in the north (Schleswig-Holstein, Lower Saxony), North Rhine-Westphalia and Bavaria, sometimes in Baden-Württemberg and rarely in Hesse.

de-lm-440431.title: Bollard: Thuringia plates split by a black line
de-lm-440431.summary: Thuringia's triangular post plates are unique, with sections split by a black line.

de-lm-440433.title: Bollard: plain white plate
de-lm-440433.summary: Basic white plates on bollards are found in all states except Bavaria, Saarland and the city states.

de-lm-445858.title: Street sign: white, all capitals
de-lm-445858.summary: Darmstadt's white street signs are often written in ALL CAPS, which is unique in the country.

de-n3r2.title: Sign: bike direction signs, green or red text
de-n3r2.summary: Bicycle direction signs are white with green text. In Hamburg, North Rhine-Westphalia and a nearby part of Lower Saxony the text is red. Saarland has white text on dark green.

de-njj7.title: Bollard: standing on a black disk
de-njj7.summary: Bollards standing on black disks are common across eastern Germany.

de-np9D.title: Pole: triangle tops, like Czechia and Slovakia
de-np9D.summary: Triangle pole tops like those in Czechia and Slovakia are common in the west, with some exceptions.

de-o1vB.title: Houses: big socialist-era apartment blocks
de-o1vB.summary: Large, plain apartment blocks from the socialist era are common across the former East.

de-pJU0.title: Route marker: blue autobahn km marker
de-pJU0.summary: Blue rectangular km markers with a white border are on motorways. Other roads have white markers with a black border, and small roads triangular ones.

de-rNPD.title: Bollard: irregular, no white lower half
de-rNPD.summary: Odd bollards without a white lower half are on K-roads in a part of Lower Saxony. K-roads there have no other bollard type.

de-sp9A.title: Trees: white paint near the base, northeast
de-sp9A.summary: Trees painted white near the bottom of the trunk are in the northeast, rarely outside.

de-sviz.title: Bins: each city state has its own
de-sviz.summary: Berlin: bright orange bins with white text. Hamburg: bright red with white speech bubbles. Bremen: green and grey with orange speech bubbles. Bremerhaven: plain green with a black logo.

de-uRqh.title: Bollard: orange plates
de-uRqh.summary: The only state where bollard plates are orange instead of white.

de-ucwE.title: Bollard: grey plates
de-ucwE.summary: The only state where bollard plates can be grey instead of white.

de-vbHB.title: Pole: white rectangular sticker on wood
de-vbHB.summary: Most wooden poles carry a white rectangular sticker.

de-vfTH.title: Houses: brick houses in the northwest
de-vfTH.summary: Brick houses are mostly in the northwest. The map is approximate.

de-vzOg.title: Route marker: metal border around the marker
de-vzOg.summary: Markers with a metal border are in Schleswig-Holstein and Lower Saxony. The numbers after the comma are usually smaller in Lower Saxony.

de-wnBA.title: Bus stop: each city state has its own
de-wnBA.summary: Berlin: segmented stops on a yellow post. Hamburg: red post with route numbers in hexagons. Bremen: simple stops with the name in a red section. Bremerhaven: grey section on the back of the post and the name in red on yellow.

de-y24J.title: Houses: thatched roofs, rock walls, north coast
de-y24J.summary: Thatched roofs and stone walls are most common on the North Frisian Islands and the northern mainland coast, and in coastal resort towns in the northeast.

de-ygrs.title: Pole: trident-like tops
de-ygrs.summary: Trident-shaped pole tops are found in Bavaria, Saxony-Anhalt and Baden-Württemberg.
